name: Magicoder OSS-Instruct 75K
size: ~75K instruction-response pairs (per dataset name and paper)
summary: Synthetic instructions generated by prompting an LLM with random open-source code snippets (OSS-Instruct) to reduce the bias of purely LLM-invented tasks.
how_to_use: Good diverse seed for general code SFT; pair with Evol-style data (the paper reports the two are complementary). Check overlap before mixing with CodeFeedback, which re-uses it.
caveats: Card states it was generated by gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 and warns to follow OpenAI's usage policy. No execution verification of solutions. Seeds come from public GitHub code.

name: Magicoder Evol-Instruct 110K
summary: Decontaminated version of theblackcat102/evol-codealpaca-v1 (WizardCoder-style Evol-Instruct on Code Alpaca seeds), decontaminated with the StarCoder/BigCode procedure.
how_to_use: Use as the cleaner copy of the Evol-CodeAlpaca lineage. Combine with OSS-Instruct for a Magicoder-S style mix.
caveats: Parent data was generated with gpt-4-0314 and gpt-4-0613 (per the evol-codealpaca-v1 card), so OpenAI terms apply. Decontamination covers older benchmarks only; recheck against newer evals.

name: Evol-CodeAlpaca v1
size: 100K-1M rows (HF size category); exact count not verified
summary: Open re-creation of the WizardCoder Evol-Instruct code data: Code Alpaca 20K evolved with 10 augmentation strategies and answered by GPT-4.
how_to_use: Prefer the decontaminated Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110K copy for training; use this one for lineage or research.
caveats: Card says gpt-4-0314 and gpt-4-0613 produced the evolutions and answers (OpenAI terms apply). Not decontaminated against modern benchmarks in this original form.

name: Evol-Instruct-Code-80k-v1
summary: Community replication of the WizardCoder Evol-Instruct code data.
how_to_use: Research use only because of the non-commercial license. Prefer evol-codealpaca-v1 or the Magicoder copy for commercial work.
caveats: Non-commercial license. Generated with OpenAI models (not verified from the card; the card is minimal).

name: Code Alpaca 20K
summary: Self-Instruct-style code instruction set that started the open code-instruction line; seed of Evol-CodeAlpaca.
how_to_use: Mostly historical. Small, noisy and easy; useful as a seed for evolution, not as a main SFT source.
caveats: Project README says it was generated with Self-Instruct techniques and notes OpenAI TOS (text-davinci-003 per the Self-Instruct recipe; model name not confirmed on the card). Short, simple tasks; saturated.

name: CodeFeedback-Filtered-Instruction
summary: 287K queries from Magicoder-OSS, Python ShareGPT, Magicoder-Evol and Evol-Instruct, filtered to complexity 4-5 by Qwen-72B-Chat.
how_to_use: Use when you want a complexity-filtered union of earlier instruction sets instead of the raw parents.
caveats: Card warns that part of the data was generated by OpenAI models. Overlaps heavily with Magicoder data. Filter used a model-assigned complexity score, not execution.

name: Code-Feedback (OpenCodeInterpreter)
summary: Multi-turn code data with execution feedback and human-feedback-style follow-ups for iterative refinement (OpenCodeInterpreter).
how_to_use: Include if you want a model that reads execution output and fixes its code over several turns.
caveats: Card says part of it was generated by GPT-4-0613 and GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 (OpenAI usage policy applies). The headline 91.6 HumanEval/MBPP average in the paper used synthesized GPT-4 feedback at inference.

name: StarCoder2 self-oss-instruct (SelfCodeAlign data)
summary: Instruction data produced by StarCoder2-15B itself via the SelfCodeAlign pipeline (concept extraction, task generation, sampled responses with tests, execution filter). Used for StarCoder2-15B-Instruct.
how_to_use: One of the few permissively usable SFT sets with no proprietary teacher; good default when you must avoid OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepSeek-derived outputs.
caveats: Python only. The paper describes a transparent pipeline without distillation from a stronger model. Quality is bounded by the base model that generated it.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('bigcode/self-oss-instruct-sc2-exec-filter-50k', split='train')
# columns: instruction, response, prompt, seed, sha1, fingerprint, id

name: CommitPackFT
license: MIT (HF card tag); per-file source licenses are permissive
summary: Filtered subset of CommitPack where commit messages resemble natural-language instructions; basis of OctoPack/OctoCoder instruction tuning.
how_to_use: Use for code-edit style instructions from real human commits with no LLM teacher. Per-language configs.
caveats: Commit messages are noisy even after filtering. Predates modern evals. Contamination with benchmark repos should be checked.

name: CommitPack
license: MIT (HF card tag); per-file source licenses are permissive
summary: Raw commit corpus (code before/after plus message) from which CommitPackFT was filtered.
how_to_use: Use when you want to build your own commit-based edit data or commit-message models. Most SFT users want CommitPackFT instead.
caveats: Very large and noisy. Not a download for low-resource machines.

name: EditPackFT
summary: Further-filtered CommitPackFT subset formatted for instructional code editing (before code, instruction, after code), used to train CanItEdit-evaluated models.
how_to_use: Use to teach instruction-following code edits; evaluate with CanItEdit.
caveats: Small. Derived from commit messages, so instruction quality varies.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nuprl/EditPackFT', split='train')
# columns include: instruction, old_contents, new_contents, lang, commit

name: CanItEdit
summary: Hand-written benchmark for instructional code editing with descriptive and lazy instructions and hidden tests. Included here as the matching eval for EditPackFT-style training.
how_to_use: Use as a held-out eval for edit training; do not train on it.
caveats: Tiny, so noisy. Released in 2023 and may be in newer training mixes.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nuprl/CanItEdit', split='test')  # columns: before, after, tests, instruction_descriptive, instruction_lazy

name: OpenCoder opc-sft-stage1
size: 3 configs: filtered_infinity_instruct, largescale_diverse_instruct, realuser_instruct; row counts not read
summary: Stage-1 SFT mix of OpenCoder: filtered general instructions plus large-scale synthetic and real-user code instructions.
how_to_use: Use as broad general-plus-code instruction data in a two-stage SFT recipe (general first, then code-heavy stage 2).
caveats: Real-user part is extracted from ShareGPT/WildChat-style conversations, so it inherits their provenance and OpenAI-model responses (card says low-quality responses were regenerated; the generator model was not confirmed).

name: OpenCoder opc-sft-stage2
size: 4 configs: educational_instruct 118,278; evol_instruct 111,183; mceval_instruct 35,943; package_instruct 170,943 (dataset_info, split row counts)
summary: High-quality stage-2 code SFT: educational synthetic, evolved, McEval-style multilingual and package-usage instructions.
how_to_use: Use as the code-focused second SFT stage; the paper's recipe pairs it with stage 1.
caveats: Teacher models per subset not confirmed from the card. Check for overlap with Evol-Instruct and Magicoder.

name: Glaive Code Assistant v3
summary: Synthetic code Q&A from Glaive's data platform; v3 includes v1 and v2.
how_to_use: Cheap breadth for chat-style coding help; filter hard before using as a main source.
caveats: Card does not name the generator model, so teacher provenance and terms are unknown. No execution verification stated.

name: Ling-Coder-SFT
summary: Subset of the SFT data used for Ling-Coder-Lite, synthesized with OSS-Instruct and Evol-Instruct style pipelines.
how_to_use: Large synthetic code SFT with Chinese coverage; sample and filter rather than use whole.
caveats: Card does not name the generator models, so provenance and terms are unclear. Not execution-verified per the card.

name: OpenCodeInstruct (NVIDIA)
size: 5,000,000 instruction-solution rows with unit tests, execution status and LLM judgments
summary: Largest open code instruction set: each row has question, solution, generated unit tests, execution results and an LLM quality assessment, so you can filter by test score.
how_to_use: Filter on average_test_score and llm_judgement before SFT; do not train on all 5M blindly. Stream it, it is ~19 GB uncompressed.
caveats: Per the paper, solutions, tests and judgments came from Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (Qwen license terms apply to outputs). Tests are model-written, so a passing row is not guaranteed correct. Python-centric.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nvidia/OpenCodeInstruct', split='train', streaming=True)
# columns: id, input, output, domain, generation_algorithm, llm_judgement, unit_tests, tests_execution_status, average_test_score

name: OpenCodeReasoning (NVIDIA, v1)
summary: DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces and solutions for competitive problems from TACO, APPS, CodeContests and open-r1/codeforces, used to train OCR-Qwen models via SFT only.
how_to_use: Strong SFT source for competitive-programming reasoning. The paper reports 61.8 LiveCodeBench for its best distilled model with SFT only; the paper's own ablation found execution filtering hurt benchmark accuracy, so prioritize instruction diversity.
caveats: Responses generated by DeepSeek-R1 (MIT-licensed model; card labels data CC-BY-4.0). Questions come from third-party sites, so the card has a per-row license column to check. Correctness is not execution-verified.

name: OpenCodeReasoning-2 (NVIDIA)
size: dataset_info lists 1,398,166 and 1,174,475 rows (two splits; split names and languages not re-checked)
summary: Second release: R1 generations with QwQ critiques and right/wrong judgements, for both code completion and code critique SFT.
how_to_use: Use for reasoning SFT plus critique training; the pass_rate and judgement columns allow filtering.
caveats: Generations by DeepSeek-R1 and critiques by QwQ-32B (per card fields r1_generation, qwq_critique). Judgement labels are model-produced, not ground truth.

name: Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v1 (code split)
size: code split 1,896,395 rows (dataset_info); also chat 746,622, math 2,044,407, stem 20,662,167, tool_calling 310,051
summary: SFT compilation behind Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1.5 with reasoning on/off responses; the code split carries reasoning traces.
how_to_use: Load only the code split and filter; it has a reasoning flag so you can build mixed think/no-think data.
caveats: Card lists teachers including DeepSeek-R1-0528 and Qwen3-235B-A22B, so those model terms apply. Large; stream it.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nvidia/Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v1', split=['code'], streaming=True)

name: Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset (code)
license: CC-BY-4.0 (card also notes Llama-derived-data redistribution requirements)
size: SFT code split 10,108,883 samples (card table); also math, science, chat and RL configs
summary: Post-training data for Llama-3.3-Nemotron-70B and Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B; v1.1 added 500K code reasoning samples.
how_to_use: Use the SFT/code split with its reasoning on/off labels; subsample heavily.
caveats: Teachers include DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-72B, Llama-3.3-70B and Mixtral-8x22B per the card; parts are subject to Llama license redistribution terms. Very large.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nvidia/Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset', 'SFT', split=['code'], streaming=True)

name: Nemotron-SFT-Competitive-Programming-v2
size: 336K+ Python and 332K+ C++ samples over 34,799 questions; 40K Exercism-derived; 96.5K text-to-SQL with reasoning (card)
summary: Competitive coding with reasoning and critique, Python Exercism-style exercises (Aider problems decontaminated), and enterprise text-to-SQL records generated with NVIDIA Data Designer.
how_to_use: Pick the subset you need: competitive for reasoning, Exercism for exercise-style, SQL for schema-linking reasoning.
caveats: Card names DeepSeek-R1-0528 as a generator for the competitive subset; SQL generator not confirmed in the text read. Problem sources have their own licenses.

name: Nemotron-SFT-OpenCode-v1
size: 100K-1M rows (HF size category; exact count not read)
summary: Agentic instruction data for the OpenCode CLI: tool calling, AGENTS.md prompts, agent skills, bash-only tools and clarifying-question tool, in six subsets.
how_to_use: Use to teach CLI-agent tool use and skills loading; match the harness format (OpenCode) at inference.
caveats: Per card, questions and skills were synthesized with GPT OSS 120B and solution traces with Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, so those terms apply. Tied to one harness format.

name: Nemotron-SFT-SWE-v2
license: CC-BY-4.0 plus Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD (API list)
size: ~46K OpenHands agent trajectories plus agentless localization, repair and test-generation subset (card)
summary: SWE-Bench-style data: OpenHands agentic trajectories and agentless sub-task SFT data built from SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-reBench, SWE-Smith and SWE-Fixer-Train.
how_to_use: Use both halves: trajectories for agent behavior, agentless data for localization/repair/test-writing skills.
caveats: Agentic trajectories generated by Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct; agentless responses by DeepSeek-R1-0528 (card). Mostly Python repositories; source issue data has own licenses.

name: Nemotron-Cascade-SFT-SWE
size: size not read (card has per-source question and sample tables)
summary: Agentless-mini style SWE SFT data (localization, repair, test generation) from SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-reBench and SWE-Smith, difficulty-selected and decontaminated against SWE-Bench Verified repos.
how_to_use: Use for non-agentic SWE skills; card reports 37.2 and 43.1 resolve rates for 8B and 14B models after SFT and RL (card, 2026-11-24).
caveats: Responses generated with DeepSeek-R1-0528. Excludes repositories present in SWE-Bench Verified, which limits but does not remove all contamination risk elsewhere.

name: Nemotron-Agentic-Tool-Use-v1
summary: Multi-turn tool-use conversations: interactive-agent trajectories (simulated user, agent, tool environment) and general tool-calling, judge-filtered.
how_to_use: Use for generic tool-calling skill alongside coding data.
caveats: Tool-calling subset uses Qwen3-235B-A22B Thinking and Instruct 2507 per the card; other subset generators not fully read. LLM-judge filtered, tools are simulated.

name: open-r1 CodeForces-CoTs
size: ~10K Codeforces problems with up to 5 R1 traces each; many configs (solutions, solutions_py, decontaminated variants)
summary: DeepSeek-R1 chain-of-thought solutions in C++ and Python for Codeforces problems, used to train OlympicCoder.
how_to_use: Use the decontaminated configs (solutions_decontaminated or solutions_py_decontaminated) for training.
caveats: Traces generated by DeepSeek-R1. Problems are from Codeforces. Not all traces are verified correct unless using the verified configs; check the card.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('open-r1/codeforces-cots', 'solutions_decontaminated')

name: open-r1 Mixture-of-Thoughts (code)
license: not stated in API tags (check card)
size: 350K verified R1 traces total; code config 83,070 rows (dataset_info)
summary: Verified DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces across math, code and science; code part is competitive-programming focused.
how_to_use: Load the code config for code-only reasoning SFT.
caveats: Traces distilled from DeepSeek-R1. License field absent in the API tags, so confirm terms before commercial use.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('open-r1/Mixture-of-Thoughts', 'code', split='train')

name: OpenThoughts-114k
summary: DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces with correctness verification; code rows include test cases and starter code.
how_to_use: Historic open R1-distillation set; superseded by OpenThoughts3.
caveats: Generated by DeepSeek-R1. Code is a minority of the mix.

name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
summary: Result of 1,000+ controlled data-recipe experiments; each question annotated 16x with QwQ-32B. Trains OpenThinker3-7B.
how_to_use: Take the code slice (domain column) for reasoning SFT; the paper is also the best public source on which pipeline choices matter.
caveats: Teacher is QwQ-32B (Apache-2.0 model). Not execution-verified per row. Paper reports 51% LiveCodeBench for the 7B model (arxiv abstract).

name: OpenThoughts-Agent-v1-SFT
summary: Teacher-agent traces on nl2bash and InferredBugs (C# and Java bugs) tasks, in the Terminus-2 harness, used for OpenThinker-Agent-v1.
how_to_use: Small, terminal-agent oriented SFT set; pair with its RL tasks.
caveats: Traces generated with GLM-4.6 (AWQ quant) per the card. Only two task families, so narrow.

name: Bespoke-Stratos-17k
summary: DeepSeek-R1 distillation of the Sky-T1 recipe (code, math, science, puzzles) used for Bespoke-Stratos models; made at about $800 of generation per the card.
how_to_use: Small proof that ~17K good traces move reasoning benchmarks; mostly useful as a reference recipe.
caveats: Generated by DeepSeek-R1. Small and early; superseded by larger sets.

name: Sky-T1 data 17K
summary: Training data of Sky-T1-32B-Preview (code and math with QwQ-generated reasoning).
how_to_use: Reference recipe; small.
caveats: Card is minimal; teacher model not confirmed here.

name: rStar-Coder (Microsoft)
size: 418K problems, 580K long-reasoning solutions with test cases (card); configs synthetic_sft, synthetic_rl, synthetic_rl_testcase, seed_sft, seed_testcase
summary: Competition-level problems, with synthesized solvable problems, mutually verified input-output test cases and test-verified long-reasoning solutions; for SFT and RL.
how_to_use: Use seed_sft or synthetic_sft for SFT and the testcase configs for RL rewards; the verified test cases are the main value.
caveats: Card benchmark numbers are self-reported. Reasoning solution generator not confirmed from the lines read. Test cases for the human-seeded part are partly synthesized (is_synthesized column).

name: KodCode-V1
size: ~484K question-solution-test triplets (dataset_info train split); Instruct, Complete and Online-Judge styles
summary: Synthetic questions with self-verified solutions and pytest or stdio tests, spanning easy to hard.
how_to_use: Use verified triplets for RL rewards or SFT; the R1-response version is better for reasoning SFT.
caveats: Non-commercial license. Solutions and tests generated by gpt-4o-0513 (card), so OpenAI terms also apply.

name: KodCode-V1-SFT-R1
size: dataset_info lists 268,211 / 210,787 / 4,439 rows across splits (split names not re-checked)
summary: KodCode with DeepSeek-R1 responses kept via test-based rejection sampling; columns include r1_solution, r1_correctness and gpt_difficulty.
how_to_use: Use r1_correctness to keep only test-passing R1 responses.
caveats: Non-commercial. Questions/tests from gpt-4o-0513, responses from DeepSeek-R1 (paper abstract). Python only.

name: KodCode-Light-RL-10K
summary: Filtered 10K subset of KodCode-V1-SFT-R1 for RL (GRPO/PPO); card reports GRPO runs on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct.
how_to_use: Easy first RL set with tests; fits a single-node run.
caveats: Non-commercial. Test cases written by GPT-4o; small and Python-only.

name: Magpie-Qwen2.5-Coder-Pro-300K
summary: Raw conversations built by the Magpie self-synthesis method with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct; includes task_category, difficulty and quality columns.
how_to_use: Use the difficulty and input_quality columns to filter; no seeds needed, so cheap to regenerate with your own model.
caveats: Generated by Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (card). License tag is 'other'; check Qwen terms. Raw, unfiltered conversations.

name: Tulu 3 SFT Mixture (code parts)
license: ODC-By-1.0 overall; subsets carry other licenses, some non-commercial (card)
size: 939,343 rows total; code-heavy parts include Tulu 3 Persona Python (34,999 prompts) and Evol CodeAlpaca (107,276 prompts)
summary: General SFT mixture for Tulu 3; a template for how much code to blend into a general assistant.
how_to_use: Study the card to see the code share of a published recipe, or filter by the source column.
caveats: Mixed provenance; card warns some portions are non-commercial and that it is a research artifact. Persona Python generated by a frontier LLM (not named in the lines read).
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('allenai/tulu-3-sft-mixture', split='train')
# flattened columns per dataset_info: id, content, role, source

name: SmolTalk
license: not stated in API tags (check card)
summary: General SFT mixture used for SmolLM2 with code-containing subsets such as smol-magpie-ultra.
how_to_use: Use as the general-chat side of a mix; code share is modest.
caveats: License tag missing in the API; subsets are generated with distilabel and carry their own terms.

name: SWE-smith task instances
size: 50,137 task instances from 128 GitHub repos (card); later README says no longer updated, use SWE-smith-[lang] sets
summary: Executable synthetic SWE tasks that break existing tests, with environments; used for training agents and as RL environments.
how_to_use: Use as a source of verifiable repair tasks for RL or trajectory generation.
caveats: Python only. Maintainers say the monorepo set is no longer updated (12/14/2025 note); language-specific sets such as SWE-smith-py are maintained.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('SWE-bench/SWE-smith', split='train')
# columns: instance_id, patch, image_name, repo, problem_statement

name: SWE-smith trajectories
size: dataset_info lists splits of 24,100 / 26,076 / 25,826 rows (split names not re-checked); card says 5,017 trajectories were used to fine-tune Qwen 2.5 Coder
summary: SWE-agent trajectories with Claude 3.7 Sonnet on SWE-smith instances; columns include messages, resolved, model and patch.
how_to_use: Filter on resolved=True before SFT.
caveats: Generated by Claude 3.7 Sonnet via SWE-agent (card), so Anthropic terms apply to using outputs to train models. Python only.

name: nebius SWE-agent-trajectories
summary: SWE-agent trajectories with resolved or failed labels and patches, from a Llama-3.1-70B based agent on SWE-bench-like tasks.
how_to_use: Use success/fail labels for rejection sampling or preference pairs.
caveats: Card says to comply with the Llama 3.1 License for outputs. Older and weaker teacher than recent sets.

name: nebius SWE-rebench OpenHands trajectories
summary: OpenHands trajectories on SWE-rebench tasks generated with Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct.
how_to_use: Use the resolved subset as agent SFT data.
caveats: Teacher is Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct (card; Apache-2.0 model).

name: SWE-Gym OpenHands sampled trajectories
license: not stated in API tags (check card)
summary: OpenHands trajectories sampled on SWE-Gym tasks with a resolved flag, with trajectory-level resolved labels.
how_to_use: Filter by resolved; small.
caveats: No license tag. Teacher model not confirmed from the lines read. Small.

name: gretelai/synthetic_text_to_sql
summary: Synthetic text-to-SQL with schemas, prompts, SQL and explanations across many SQL task types.
how_to_use: Cheap breadth for SQL SFT; mix with execution-grounded data.
caveats: Made with Gretel Navigator; card mentions GPT-4 was used to score quality, generator not confirmed. Not execution-validated against real databases.

name: SynSQL-2.5M
summary: Million-scale synthetic cross-domain text-to-SQL used to train the OmniSQL models.
how_to_use: Largest open text-to-SQL set; subsample and mix with Spider and BIRD training data as OmniSQL did.
caveats: Generator models not confirmed from the lines read. Synthetic databases differ from messy production schemas.

name: Spider (text-to-SQL)
summary: Human-annotated cross-domain text-to-SQL; columns db_id, query, question.
how_to_use: Classic training and dev set; saturated for frontier models.
caveats: Share-alike license. Saturated and widely contaminated; execution needs the separate database files.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('xlangai/spider')  # columns: db_id, query, question

name: CodeUltraFeedback
size: 10,000 instructions with 4 responses each from a 14-LLM pool (paper)
summary: Preference data: coding instructions with responses ranked on five coding preferences by GPT-3.5 as judge, with scores and textual feedback.
how_to_use: Use for DPO on style and instruction-following preferences (readability, efficiency, etc.), not for correctness.
caveats: Labels are from a GPT-3.5 judge (paper), so noisy and not execution-based; responses include GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 outputs (OpenAI terms). Small.

name: AceCode-87K (TIGER-Lab)
size: 87,149 questions with ~16 filtered test cases each and scored model completions (card)
summary: Questions rewritten by GPT-4o-mini with synthesized test cases; includes completions with pass rates, used for reward models and RL (AceCoder).
how_to_use: Build pass-rate preference pairs yourself, or use the ready-made AceCodePair-300K; also usable as RL prompts with tests.
caveats: Questions and tests rewritten by GPT-4o-mini (OpenAI terms). Test cases are LLM-synthesized and filtered, so imperfect. Completion model names are in a model_name column.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('TIGER-Lab/AceCode-87K', split='train')
# columns: id, source, question, test_cases, inferences

name: AceCodePair-300K (TIGER-Lab)
size: 100K-1M rows (size category); exact count not read
summary: Test-case-derived preference pairs built from AceCode-87K pass rates, used to train AceCode reward models with Bradley-Terry loss.
how_to_use: Use for reward-model training or DPO on correctness preferences. AceCoder reports best-of-32 gains of ~10 points for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and ~5 for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (paper abstract).
caveats: Pairs inherit GPT-4o-mini rewritten tests from AceCode-87K, which can be wrong. Column names not read from the card.

name: AceCode-V2-122K (TIGER-Lab)
summary: Improved AceCode: questions and tests rewritten by OpenAI o1-mini and filtered with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct; card includes RL results for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Base.
how_to_use: Use as RL prompts with test rewards, or sample from your own model and build pass-rate pairs.
caveats: Rewrites by o1-mini (OpenAI terms). Card benchmark numbers are self-reported.

name: Ling-Coder-DPO
summary: Code DPO pairs derived from CodeContests, choosing positive and negative samples by test pass rate, perplexity distribution and reward-model score.
how_to_use: Larger test-pass-based DPO set from a real production recipe.
caveats: Source problems are CodeContests; response generator models not named in the lines read.

name: Qwen3-Coder-Next OpenCode Preference
summary: DPO pairs from rejection sampling: 8 samples per problem, chosen passes 100% of tests, rejected fails, with labeled rejection types. Companion to an SFT set of 49,374 examples.
how_to_use: Test-verified on-policy-style pairs for competitive programming; hard-negative configs listed on the card.
caveats: Third-party release by an individual; generated with Qwen3-Coder-Next (Qwen terms). Small.

name: Vezora Code-Preference-Pairs
summary: DPO-style pairs from the Open-Critic-GPT synthetic pipeline: code with inserted bugs as the rejected side.
how_to_use: Use only for bug-awareness contrast; low-cost synthetic.
caveats: Synthetic bug injection, so rejected samples are artificial and unlike natural model errors; teacher model not confirmed from the lines read; license tag 'other'. Third-party release.

name: Skywork-OR1-RL-Data
